title: Interaction of the Gut Microbiota and the Enteric Nervous System: Implications in Gastrointestinal Disorders Associated With Autism Spectrum Disorder.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impairments in social interaction, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors. In addition to these core behavioral symptoms, gastrointestinal (GI) disorders are frequently reported, ranging from severe constipation to diarrhea. The links between ASD and gut dysfunction are further supported by alterations in gut microbiota composition and in bacteria-derived metabolites. As the intrinsic nervous system of the digestive tract, the enteric nervous system (ENS) plays a central role in gut physiology by exerting neuronal control on several gut functions, including motility. Located at the interface between the gut microbiota and intestinal function, the ENS may play a key role in the GI symptoms associated with ASD, as demonstrated in several mouse models. This review aims to summarize the interconnected alterations of the gut microbiota and the ENS in ASD, with a particular focus on the microbiota-derived mediators that are altered in ASD, among patients and animal models, and that may affect ENS development and function. By highlighting these interactions, this review seeks to provide new insights on the digestive pathophysiology of ASD, which may also contribute to the severity of behavioral symptoms.
authors: Ganachaud B, Mendoza-León MJ, Marchix J, Tello AF, Scoul CLB, Opazo MC, Neunlist M, Riedel CA, Caillaud M, Boudin H.
journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
screening_reason: The paper directly reviews the interaction between the gut microbiota and the enteric nervous system (ENS) in the context of autism spectrum disorder.
summary_ja: 本文献は、自閉スペクトラム症（ASD）における腸内細菌叢と腸管神経系（ENS）の相互作用およびその変化についてまとめたレビューである。ASD患者や動物モデルにおいて変化している細菌由来のメディエーターが、ENSの発達や機能にどのように影響を及ぼすかに焦点を当てている。これらの相互作用を明らかにすることで、ASDに伴う消化器症状の病態生理の理解を深め、行動症状の重症度との関連性についても新たな知見を提供する。
summary_en: This review summarizes the interconnected alterations of the gut microbiota and the enteric nervous system (ENS) in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). It focuses on microbiota-derived mediators that are altered in ASD patients and animal models and how they affect ENS development and function. Understanding these interactions provides new insights into the digestive pathophysiology of ASD and its potential impact on behavioral symptoms.
key_finding_ja: ASDにおける腸内細菌叢由来のメディエーターの変化が、腸管神経系（ENS）の発達や機能に影響を与え、消化器症状や行動症状に関与している可能性が示唆されている。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢と腸管神経系の相互作用を解明することは、自閉スペクトラム症に伴う消化器症状および行動症状に対する新たな治療アプローチの開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Wastewater-Based Human Gut Microbiome Surveillance Links Microbial Signatures to Population Health in Ohio Communities.
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has been widely used to track infectious diseases, yet its potential for population-level gut microbiome surveillance and broader public health assessment remains limited. Here, we present a multi-city study in Ohio, USA, demonstrating how sewage-derived human gut microbiome profiles can be leveraged to infer community health patterns. In this retrospective cross-sectional study, influent wastewater samples were collected from eight Ohio cities (May - June 2022). Community-level gut bacterial profiles were characterized and integrated with publicly available health, lifestyle, socioeconomic, and demographic data using geospatial analysis. Bioinformatic processing and multivariate statistical approaches, including principal component analysis and multiple linear regressions, were used to examine associations between microbial features and population health indicators. Distinct microbial signatures were observed across cities, including variation in clinically relevant taxa such as Bacteroidota, Desulfobacterota, Verrucomicrobiota, Akkermansia, Desulfovibrio, and Streptococcus. Several microbial features, including Firmicutes, Desulfovibrio, Acetobacterium, and alpha diversity, were significantly associated with indicators of chronic disease burden and health-related factors, including smoking, obesity, unemployment, and minority status. Notably, several microbial variables demonstrated statistical associations with multiple community health metrics (e.g., hypertension, high cholesterol, asthma, obesity, smoking, depression, and unemployment), and rural communities generally exhibited higher adverse health burdens alongside distinct microbiome profiles. These findings highlight the feasibility of integrating wastewater-based gut microbiome data with demographic and health indicators to evaluate community health disparities. This study expands the scope of WBE beyond infectious disease monitoring and supports its application in informing targeted and equitable public health interventions.
authors: Lancaster E, Lee J.
screening_reason: The study investigates population-level human gut microbiome profiles and gut bacterial signatures in relation to health.
summary_ja: 本研究は、米国オハイオ州の8つの都市から採取した下水サンプルを用いて、地域社会レベルのヒト腸内細菌叢プロファイルを評価した。得られた細菌叢データと、公開されている健康、ライフスタイル、社会経済、人口統計データを地理空間分析および多変量統計解析を用いて統合した。その結果、Firmicutes門やDesulfovibrio属、Acetobacterium属、およびα多様性が、肥満、高血圧、うつ病、失業などの慢性疾患負担や健康関連因子と有意に関連していることが示された。特に地方のコミュニティでは、健康被害の負担が高く、特徴的な細菌叢プロファイルが観察された。
summary_en: This study utilized wastewater-based epidemiology to monitor community-level human gut microbiome profiles across eight cities in Ohio, USA. By integrating sewage-derived microbial data with public health, socioeconomic, and demographic indicators, the researchers identified distinct microbial signatures associated with chronic disease burdens. Specific microbial features, such as Firmicutes, Desulfovibrio, and alpha diversity, were significantly linked to health-related factors including obesity, hypertension, and depression. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of using wastewater surveillance to assess population-level health disparities.
key_finding_ja: 下水由来の腸内細菌叢プロファイルが、肥満や高血圧、うつ病などの地域社会における慢性疾患の負担や社会経済的指標と有意に関連していることを明らかにした。
why_it_matters_ja: 下水ベースの疫学調査を感染症監視だけでなく腸内細菌叢を介した地域住民の健康状態や格差の評価にまで拡張することで、より効果的で公平な公衆衛生介入の立案に寄与する可能性があります。

title: Long-term antibiotics treatment-induced anxiety-like behavior is associated with disrupted colonic tryptophan metabolism.
abstract: The widespread and often excessive use of antibiotics has raised concerns about its long-term impact on host health. Growing evidence suggests that antibiotics-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis may contribute to neuropsychiatric conditions, including anxiety. However, the mechanistic pathways linking chronic antibiotic exposure, microbial disruption, and anxiety-like behaviors remain largely unclear. To investigate the effects of antibiotic exposure on gut-brain axis function, mice were administered antibiotic-containing drinking water for either short-term or long-term durations. Behavioral assessments, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, biochemical analyses, histological staining, and Western blotting were used to evaluate anxiety-like behaviors, microbiota composition, tryptophan (Trp) metabolism, intestinal barrier integrity, and inflammation in both the colon and hippocampus. Long-term, but not short-term, antibiotic treatment induced pronounced anxiety-like behaviors in mice. Microbiota analysis revealed that long-term antibiotic exposure significantly reduced microbial diversity and altered the abundance of key bacterial genera. These changes were associated with disrupted colonic Trp metabolism, reflected by decreased Trp and 5-HT levels in the colon and serum, along with suppressed expression of the Trp metabolic enzyme TPH1 and 5-HT4R. Additionally, long-term antibiotic treatment impaired intestinal barrier integrity, downregulated tight junction proteins and MUC2, and activated colonic TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammatory signaling pathways. Neuroinflammation was also observed in the hippocampus. Our results reveal a time-dependent effect of antibiotic-induced anxiety-like behaviors and suggest that gut microbiota dysbiosis, disrupted colonic Trp metabolism, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and neuroinflammation may collectively contribute to the behavioral alterations associated with long-term antibiotic exposure. These findings provide new insights into the gut-brain mechanisms underlying microbiota-associated mood disorders.
authors: Wu J, Li T, Wang A, Li MA, Song YZ, Hu R, Tao Y, Qiao CM, Cui C, Zhao WJ, Shen YQ.
screening_reason: The paper examines how antibiotic-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis and disrupted colonic tryptophan metabolism lead to hippocampal neuroinflammation and anxiety-like behavior.
summary_ja: マウスへの長期的な抗生物質投与は、短期投与とは異なり、顕著な不安様行動を誘発した。この行動変化は、腸内細菌叢の多様性低下や、大腸におけるトリプトファン代謝の破壊（トリプトファンや5-HTレベルの低下など）と関連していた。さらに、長期の抗生物質投与は腸管バリア機能を損ない、大腸および海馬における炎症経路を活性化させることが示された。
summary_en: Long-term, but not short-term, antibiotic treatment in mice induced pronounced anxiety-like behaviors. This behavioral change was associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis and disrupted colonic tryptophan metabolism, including decreased tryptophan and 5-HT levels. Additionally, long-term treatment impaired intestinal barrier integrity and triggered inflammatory pathways in both the colon and the hippocampus.
key_finding_ja: マウスにおける長期的な抗生物質投与は、腸内細菌叢の乱れ、大腸のトリプトファン代謝異常、腸管バリア機能障害、および海馬の神経炎症を伴う不安様行動を誘発する。
why_it_matters_ja: 抗生物質の長期使用が精神健康に及ぼす潜在的な悪影響とその生物学的メカニズムの解明につながる可能性がある。

title: Inhalation of cadmium oxide nanoparticles alters intestinal and pulmonary microbiomes in mice.
abstract: Exposure to cadmium (Cd), a toxic heavy metal, is a severe threat to organismal health, causing a wide range of pathological alterations in various tissues and organs. Alterations in the composition and function of the gut microbiome have been indicated across numerous animals exposed to Cd. However, the impact of Cd inhalation exposure on the pulmonary microbiome has not been well investigated yet. Therefore, in this study, we investigated the effects of exposure to CdONPs and its clearance on both colonic and pulmonary microbiomes in mice. The diversity of both colonic and pulmonary microbiomes of exposed mice was significantly affected after 9 weeks of CdONPs inhalation. The effects of CdONPs exposure on bacterial composition and function were more pronounced in the colonic microbiome than in the pulmonary microbiome. The clearance was more efficient in the restoration of gut microbiome composition in comparison to the lung microbiome. Moreover, we evaluated a bidirectional interaction between Cd exposure and gut microbiota. Duncaniella, Odoribacter, and Pontibacter were the prominent biomarkers that significantly positively correlated with dysregulated functions in the colonic microbiome of exposed mice. Based on the PICRUSt2 prediction analysis, our results suggested that perturbations in the gut microbiota balance due to Cd exposure were associated with the increase in the proportion level of bacteria with excessive membrane transporters, which may potentially augment the absorption of this metal by intestinal microbiota thereby leading to the accumulation of Cd in intestinal bacteria and the potential alleviation of the Cd toxicity effect. Furthermore, genes related to metal chelators were consistent with the colonic microbiome of exposed mice, suggesting possible promotion of Cd excretion and its eventual fecal elimination. However, these observations derived from 16S rRNA profiling and PICRUSt2 predictions would need to be verified experimentally to establish any functional or mechanistic implications. This could be considered a key factor in determining the intestinal bacterial species able to minimize the toxicity of heavy metals in future therapeutic approaches. KEY POINTS: • Inhalation of CdO nanoparticles significantly alters both gut and pulmonary microbiome composition and diversity in mice. • Microbiome changes are more pronounced in the gut than in the lungs following inhalation exposure. • Partial recovery of microbiome composition occurs after the clearance period, with greater restoration in the gut than in the lung. • Predicted functional profiles indicate shifts in microbial metabolic potential associated with Cd exposure. • The findings support a potential interaction between inhaled Cd exposure and the gut microbiome, highlighting the relevance of the gut-lung axis.
authors: Mekadim C, Kristeková D, Mikuška P, Buchtová M, Mrázek J.
screening_reason: The study investigates the effects of cadmium inhalation on the composition, diversity, and metabolic function of the colonic (gut) microbiome in mice.
summary_ja: 本研究は、酸化カドミウムナノ粒子（CdONPs）の吸入暴露およびその後の排除が、マウスの結腸および肺の微生物叢に及ぼす影響を調査した。CdONPsの吸入は両部位の微生物叢の多様性と組成を著しく変化させたが、その影響は肺よりも結腸でより顕著であり、排除後の回復も結腸の方が効率的であった。予測機能解析により、腸内細菌叢の変化が金属輸送やキレートに関連する遺伝子の増加を伴い、カドミウムの蓄積や排泄を促進して毒性を軽減する可能性が示唆された。
summary_en: This study investigated the effects of inhaling cadmium oxide nanoparticles (CdONPs) and subsequent clearance on the colonic and pulmonary microbiomes of mice. Inhalation of CdONPs significantly altered the diversity and composition of both microbiomes, with more pronounced changes and more efficient recovery observed in the gut. Predicted functional profiles suggested that alterations in the gut microbiota might be associated with increased metal absorption and excretion, potentially mitigating cadmium toxicity.
key_finding_ja: 酸化カドミウムナノ粒子の吸入はマウスの結腸および肺の微生物叢を変化させ、特に結腸において顕著な組成変化と排除後の部分的な回復、および重金属毒性を軽減し得る代謝機能の変化が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 吸入された有害物質が肺だけでなく腸内細菌叢にも影響を及ぼし、さらに腸内細菌がその毒性軽減に関与する可能性を示したことは、環境汚染物質の生体影響評価や治療法の開発において重要である。

title: Immunometabolic reprogramming in multiple sclerosis: from pathogenic amplifier to therapeutic target in neuroinflammation and remyelination.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) has conventionally been considered a prototypical autoimmune disorder. While modern immunotherapies effectively control relapsing conditions, they fail to avert progressive neuroinflammation, neurodegeneration, and remyelination failure. This review offers an evidence-based recontextualization. The pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis is multifactorial, resulting from the interaction of genetic predisposition (especially HLA alleles), environmental factors (particularly Epstein-Barr virus infection), B-cell-mediated autoimmunity, and localized CNS inflammation. In this intricate environment, cellular metabolic dysregulation is a notable factor and potentially adjustable enhancer of disease progression, functioning within the extensive multifactorial pathogenic context, where the bioenergetic programming of immune and neural cells determines inflammatory or protective responses. Proinflammatory Th17 cells and M1 microglia depend on aerobic glycolysis and glutaminolysis regulated by mTOR and HIF-1α, whereas regulatory T cells, M2 microglia, and neurons require fatty acid oxidation and oxidative phosphorylation via AMPK. In multiple sclerosis, glycolysis disrupts metabolic equilibrium, sustaining chronic neuroinflammation and obstructing repair processes. Established multiple sclerosis therapies, dimethyl fumarate and teriflunomide, exhibit direct, previously unrecognized metabolic effects, validating this pathway as therapeutically viable. Emerging strategies intentionally target these vulnerabilities: glutaminase inhibitors to counteract pathogenic Th17 cells, AMPK activators such as metformin to enhance remyelination, mTOR inhibitors to restore immune tolerance, and NAD + precursors to rejuvenate mitochondrial function. Transitioning from broad immunosuppression to specific metabolic reprogramming offers remarkable opportunities for tackling chronic neuroinflammation and correcting remyelination deficits in progressive multiple sclerosis. Immuno-metabolic pharmacology is a promising field; however, its clinical application necessitates stringent validation via meticulously designed trials and dependable biomarkers.
authors: Badawi GA, El-Sayed RM, Fawzy MN.
screening_reason: The paper reviews immunometabolic reprogramming in multiple sclerosis, focusing directly on therapeutic targets to control progressive neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: 本文献は、多発性硬化症（MS）における免疫代謝の再プログラミングが、神経炎症の増幅や脱髄修復不全を駆動する重要な要因であるという観点から病態を再考したレビューである。免疫細胞や神経細胞における代謝異常（好気的解糖へのシフトなど）が慢性的な炎症を維持し、修復を阻害する仕組みを解説している。さらに、既存薬の代謝作用や、特定の代謝経路を標的とした新たな治療戦略が、進行型MSの治療において有望な選択肢となる可能性を議論している。
summary_en: This review recontextualizes multiple sclerosis (MS) by focusing on immunometabolic reprogramming as a key driver of neuroinflammation and remyelination failure. It highlights how metabolic dysregulation in immune and neural cells, such as the shift to aerobic glycolysis, sustains chronic inflammation. The authors discuss how targeting these metabolic pathways with specific agents offers promising therapeutic opportunities for progressive MS.
key_finding_ja: 多発性硬化症において、免疫細胞および神経細胞の代謝異常が慢性的な神経炎症と髄鞘再生不全を促進しており、これらを標的とした代謝再プログラミングが新たな治療標的として有望であることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 広範な免疫抑制から特定の代謝経路を標的とした治療への移行は、進行型多発性硬化症における慢性神経炎症の制御や髄鞘再生の促進に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Unique adaptations in sulfatases underpin colonic mucin degradation by Akkermansia muciniphila.
abstract: Excessive foraging of colonic mucin glycans by gut bacteria is associated with diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease. Although Akkermansia muciniphila is an important mucin degrader, the role of carbohydrate sulfatases that facilitate digestion of these heavily sulfated glycans remains unclear. Combining in vitro digestion assays, proteomics and structural biology, we show that A. muciniphila sulfatases, such as Amuc1755 and Amuc0953, have rare adaptations targeted towards known sulfated mucin structures. They show larger degrees of modularity, including a previously unknown mucin-binding domain. When grown on colonic mucin substrates, glycoproteins of reduced size were important for the growth of A. muciniphila. Further mutational analysis and localization studies revealed that desulfation of N-acetyl-D-glucosamine was periplasmic, while desulfation of D-galactose occurred extracellularly and in the periplasm. These data improve our understanding of contexts for the positive health correlations of A. muciniphila while metabolizing colonic mucin as its sole carbon source.
authors: Dey D, Salman ND, Tomlinson CWE, Jin C, Raba G, Schaus SR, Nilsson M, McIver Z, Herman R, Simpkin A, Davy M, Rigden DJ, Czjzek M, Byrne DP, Oltean M, Case A, Baumann CG, Wright GSA, van der Post S, Yates EA, Martens EC, Davey L, Luis AS, Cartmell A.
screening_reason: The paper focuses on the mechanisms of colonic mucin degradation by the gut bacterium Akkermansia muciniphila.
summary_ja: 腸内細菌であるAkkermansia muciniphilaは、大腸のムチンを分解する重要な細菌であるが、その高度に硫酸化された糖鎖の消化を促進するスルファターゼの役割は不明であった。本研究では、in vitro消化アッセイ、プロテオミクス、構造生物学を組み合わせ、Amuc1755やAmuc0953などのスルファターゼがムチン結合ドメインを含む独自の適応を有していることを明らかにした。さらに変異導入解析などにより、N-アセチル-D-グルコサミンの脱硫酸化はペリプラズムで行われ、D-ガラクトースの脱硫酸化は細胞外およびペリプラズムで行われることが示された。これらの知見は、本菌がムチンを唯一の炭素源として代謝する際の健康への好影響に関する理解を深めるものである。
summary_en: This study investigated the role of carbohydrate sulfatases in the degradation of heavily sulfated colonic mucin by the gut bacterium Akkermansia muciniphila. Using in vitro assays, proteomics, and structural biology, the researchers identified unique adaptations in sulfatases like Amuc1755 and Amuc0953, including a novel mucin-binding domain. Localization studies revealed that desulfation of N-acetyl-D-glucosamine occurs in the periplasm, whereas D-galactose desulfation occurs both extracellularly and in the periplasm. These findings enhance our understanding of how A. muciniphila utilizes colonic mucin as a carbon source.
key_finding_ja: Akkermansia muciniphilaのスルファターゼが、新規のムチン結合ドメインなどの独自の適応を有し、細胞内外の異なる部位で特定の糖の脱硫酸化を行うことを明らかにした。
why_it_matters_ja: 本菌によるムチン分解の分子メカニズムが解明されたことで、炎症性腸疾患などの病態における腸内細菌のムチン代謝の制御や、健康維持における役割の理解につながる可能性があります。

title: Lgals3high Macrophages Orchestrate Neuroinflammation and Extracellular Matrix Remodelling via NF-κB Pathway in Acute Spinal Cord Injury.
abstract: Background Acute spinal cord injury (ASCI) causes severe dysfunction, with secondary ECM remodelling being more destructive than primary injury. Macrophages regulate neuroinflammation and ECM remodelling in ASCI. Studies shown ECM related gene Lgals3 regulate macrophage polarization across various diseases. However, the role of Lgals3 in ASCI-related ECM remodelling and neuroinflammation remains unclear. Methods We integrated Single-cell RNA Sequencing (ScRNA-seq) analysis with in vitro and in vivo experiments. An ECM-related gene set was constructed for bioinformatic analyses of cell clustering, pseudotime trajectory, cell-cell communication, and transcription factor activity. LPS+IFN-γ-induced RAW264.7 macrophages were treated with the Lgals3 inhibitor GB1107, and the Lgals3/NF-κB/p65/Ccl2 axis was further dissected by siRNA-mediated Lgals3 knockdown, pharmacological NF-κB inhibition with QNZ, and TNF-α-mediated NF-κB reactivation rescue. ASCI models in SD rats were assessed via multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC), histology, TUNEL, western blot, and qRT-PCR. Results Seven cell types were identified in the ASCI microenvironment, with macrophages showing the most upregulated ECM-related genes. Four ECM-associated macrophage subtypes were defined; Lgals3 high macrophages (Mac-1), characterized by high Lgals3 and Ccl2 expression, dominated early-phase ASCI. Mac-1 exhibited the strongest intercellular communication with prominent CCL signalling pathway activation. Lgals3, Ccl2, and p65 were specifically upregulated in M1 macrophages post-ASCI, with p65 nuclear translocation. GB1107 inhibited NF-κB, promoted M1-to-M2 polarization, reduced inflammatory infiltration and ECM remodelling, and decreased apoptosis. Mechanistically, siRNA-mediated Lgals3 silencing suppressed NF-κB/p65 activation and Ccl2 expression while inducing Arg1; this phenotype was recapitulated by NF-κB inhibition and reversed by TNF-α-driven NF-κB reactivation, validating the Lgals3/NF-κB/p65/Ccl2 axis as the obligate regulatory backbone of macrophage polarization. Conclusion Lgals3 high macrophages are core drivers of ECM remodelling in ASCI via a Lgals3/NF-κB/p65/Ccl2 signalling axis that couples M1 polarization with monocyte recruitment. GB1107 disrupts this axis, reprograms macrophages from M1 to M2, attenuates inflammatory infiltration and ECM remodelling, and reduces apoptosis. GB1107 exerts therapeutic effects by regulating macrophage polarization and ECM remodelling, providing a novel "immune-matrix" dual-targeting strategy.
authors: Feng Y, Yang L, Liu Y, Pei J, Su K, Li C, Jiang H, Zhang X, Cao J, Li Y, Xie J, Cao N.
screening_reason: The study investigates how a specific macrophage subtype orchestrates neuroinflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling in acute spinal cord injury.
summary_ja: 本研究は、急性脊髄損傷（ASCI）における神経炎症と細胞外マトリックス（ECM）再構築の制御におけるLgals3高発現マクロファージの役割を明らかにした。単一細胞RNAシーケンシングおよび実験モデルを用いて、これらのマクロファージがLgals3/NF-κB/p65/Ccl2シグナル伝達軸を介して病態を駆動していることを示した。Lgals3阻害剤であるGB1107の投与は、マクロファージのM1からM2への極性変化を促進し、炎症浸潤、ECM再構築、および細胞死を減少させた。
summary_en: This study identified Lgals3-high macrophages as key regulators of neuroinflammation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling in acute spinal cord injury (ASCI). Using single-cell RNA sequencing and experimental models, the authors demonstrated that these macrophages drive pathology through the Lgals3/NF-κB/p65/Ccl2 signaling axis. Pharmacological inhibition of Lgals3 with GB1107 promoted M1-to-M2 macrophage polarization, reduced inflammatory infiltration, and attenuated ECM remodeling and apoptosis.
key_finding_ja: 急性脊髄損傷において、Lgals3高発現マクロファージがLgals3/NF-κB/p65/Ccl2軸を介して神経炎症と細胞外マトリックス再構築を主導しており、Lgals3の阻害が病態改善に有効であることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: マクロファージの極性化と細胞外マトリックス再構築を同時に標的とする「免疫-マトリックス」デュアルターゲット戦略は、急性脊髄損傷に対する新たな治療法となる可能性がある。

title: Mechanistic and functional study of lncRNA SNHG3/miR-128-3p/UBR5 axis in neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Neuroinflammation assumes a pivotal role in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis. Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate neuroinflammation through a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanism. This study aimed to explore the mechanism of SNHG3/miR-128-3p/UBR5 axis in AD associated neuroinflammation. SNHG3, miR-128-3p, and UBR5 levels were recognized by reverse transcription - quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). In vitro AD model was established by Aβ1-42 stimulation in human microglial cells HMC3 and neuronal cells SK‑N‑SH. Cell apoptosis was detected by flow cytometry. Enzyme - linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and oxidative stress indicators were used to evaluate the neuroinflammatory phenotype. Morris water maze (MWM) test assesses the spatial learning and memory abilities of amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) mice with AAV-si-SNHG3. Serum SNHG3 was clearly upregulated in AD patients, and negatively related to MMSE score (r = -0.691, P<0.001). SNHG3 had diagnostic potential for AD (AUC=0.847, 95% CI = 0.806-0.888, sensitivity=75.63%, specificity=76.88%). SNHG3 regulates UBR5 expression by sponges miR-128-3p. Silence of SNHG3 inhibited M1 polarization (reducing TNF-α, IL-6, and iNOS), promotes M2 polarization (increasing Arg1, IL-10, and TGF-β), inhibits IL-1β release, suppresses neuronal apoptosis, and mitigates oxidative stress damage (reducing MDA and increasing SOD) via miR-128-3p/UBR5 axis in Aβ-stimulated HMC3 cells. SNHG3 also contributes to Aβ‑induced neuronal apoptosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress in SK‑N‑SH cells. AAV-si-SNHG3 significantly enhances spatial learning and memory abilities of APP/PS1 mice, and inhibits neuroinflammation and oxidative stress in the hippocampus. This study is the first to elucidate that SNHG3 could regulate microglial polarization and neuroinflammation through the SNHG3/miR-128-3p/UBR5 axis.
authors: Zhu XA, Lu H, Liu Y, Xue X, Lin L.
journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
screening_reason: The study investigates the molecular mechanisms of the SNHG3/miR-128-3p/UBR5 axis in regulating microglial polarization and neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: 本研究は、アルツハイマー病（AD）に伴う神経炎症におけるlncRNA SNHG3/miR-128-3p/UBR5軸の役割を調査した。AD患者の血清においてSNHG3の発現上昇が確認され、MMSEスコアと負の相関を示した。細胞およびマウスモデルを用いた実験により、SNHG3のノックダウンがマイクログリアの極性を制御し、神経炎症や酸化ストレスを抑制するとともに、空間学習・記憶能力を向上させることが示された。
summary_en: This study investigated the role of the lncRNA SNHG3/miR-128-3p/UBR5 axis in Alzheimer's disease (AD)-associated neuroinflammation. SNHG3 expression was found to be upregulated in the serum of AD patients and negatively correlated with MMSE scores. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that silencing SNHG3 regulates microglial polarization, reduces neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, and improves spatial learning and memory in AD mouse models.
key_finding_ja: lncRNA SNHG3はmiR-128-3p/UBR5軸を介してマイクログリアの極性化と神経炎症を制御しており、その抑制はADモデルマウスの認知機能を改善する。
why_it_matters_ja: アルツハイマー病における神経炎症を標的とした新たな診断マーカーや治療法開発の基盤となる可能性がある。

title: Hippocampal endoplasmic reticulum stress drives a pro-inflammatory microglial bias and neuroinflammation in aged mice with perioperative neurocognitive disorder.
abstract: Background Perioperative neurocognitive disorder (PND) is a frequent postoperative complication in older individuals and is commonly linked to microglial activation. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress has been implicated in neuroinflammation and postoperative cognitive decline; however, whether hippocampal ER stress acts upstream to bias microglia toward a pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype, rather than serving only as a trigger of cytokine cascades, remains insufficiently defined in PND. To determine whether hippocampal ER stress promotes an M1-like microglial shift and amplifies neuroinflammation after anesthesia and surgery. Methods Eighteen-month-old male C57BL/6 mice underwent aseptic tibial fracture surgery under isoflurane anesthesia. Tauroursodeoxycholic acid（TUDCA）, a pharmacological ER stress suppressor, was delivered bilaterally into dorsal hippocampal CA1 as a perioperative mechanistic probe. ER ultrastructure in hippocampal cells was examined using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). ER stress related proteins (GRP78, p-PERK, p-eIF2ɑ, p-IRE1ɑ, ATF4, and ATF6) in hippocampus were quantified by Western blotting. Microglial phenotypic signatures were assessed by Western blotting (CD86, iNOS, CD206, ARG-1) and double immunofluorescence (CD86/Iba-1 and CD206/Iba-1). Open-field testing was performed to control for locomotion/anxiety, followed by memory assessments using novel object recognition and Morris water maze starting on postoperative day 3. Results Anesthesia and surgery induced postoperative cognitive deficits, accompanied by heightened hippocampal inflammatory signaling and a shift toward a pro-inflammatory microglial signature characterized by increased CD86 and iNOS with concomitant reductions in CD206 and ARG-1. In parallel, hippocampal ER stress activation was evident, including ER ultrastructural disruption and increased GRP78 with engagement of PERK/eIF2ɑ/ATF4-, IRE1ɑ-, and ATF6-related pathways. hippocampus-targeted delivery of TUDCA attenuated ER stress activation, mitigated the pro-inflammatory microglial shift (decreasing CD86/iNOS and restoring CD206/ARG-1), reduced inflammatory readouts, and improved postoperative memory performance. Conclusions These findings support a mechanistic link between hippocampal ER stress and the pro-inflammatory microglia bias linked to postoperative neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment in aged mice.
authors: Wang H, Tian L, Guo L, Zhao Y, Yang Z, Wu L, Lv X, Li Y.
screening_reason: The study investigates the mechanistic link between hippocampal endoplasmic reticulum stress, microglial activation, and neuroinflammation in a mouse model of perioperative neurocognitive disorder.
summary_ja: 本研究は、周術期神経認知障害（PND）の老齢マウスモデルを用いて、海馬の小胞体（ER）ストレスが炎症性ミクログリアへの偏向および神経炎症を誘発するメカニズムを調査した。麻酔および手術は、認知機能低下、海馬のERストレス活性化、および炎症性ミクログリア表現型へのシフトを引き起こした。海馬を標的としたERストレス抑制剤TUDCAの投与により、ERストレスが減弱し、炎症性ミクログリアへのシフトが抑制され、術後の記憶機能が改善した。
summary_en: This study investigated the role of hippocampal endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in driving pro-inflammatory microglial activation and neuroinflammation in aged mice with perioperative neurocognitive disorder (PND). Anesthesia and surgery induced cognitive deficits, hippocampal ER stress, and a shift toward a pro-inflammatory microglial phenotype. Targeted delivery of the ER stress suppressor TUDCA attenuated ER stress, mitigated the pro-inflammatory microglial shift, and improved postoperative memory performance.
key_finding_ja: 老齢マウスにおいて、海馬の小胞体ストレスがミクログリアの炎症性表現型への偏向を駆動し、周術期神経認知障害に伴う神経炎症と記憶障害を引き起こすことが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: 小胞体ストレスを標的とした治療介入が、高齢患者における術後認知機能障害や神経炎症を予防・改善するための新たな戦略となる可能性がある。

title: Ultrasound-Activated Piezoelectric Neuroimmune Hydrogel Orchestrates Neurogenesis-Macrophage Crosstalk in Diabetic Wound Healing.
abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds remain a major clinical challenge due to persistent inflammation, impaired neuro-immune crosstalk, and dysregulated macrophage polarization. Here, we report an injectable, ultrasound (US)-activated piezoelectric hydrogel that programmably couples neurogenesis and macrophage reprogramming to accelerate diabetic wound repair. The hydrogel is constructed from dynamic covalent networks among acyl hydrazide hyaluronic acid, benzene boronic acid modified oxidized sodium alginate, and epigallocatechin 3-gallate, and integrates a neuroactive self-assembling peptide and piezoelectric PLLA nanofibers. This design confers the hydrogel with injectability, self-healing, tissue adhesion, and US-triggered electrical signaling. In vitro, the hydrogel under US promotes M2 macrophage polarization and enhances axonal outgrowth of dorsal root ganglion neurons, establishing bidirectional neurogenesis-macrophage crosstalk. In a type II diabetic mouse model, the hydrogel markedly accelerates wound closure, elevates the M2/M1 ratio, enhances reinnervation and angiogenesis, and improves collagen remodeling. Transcriptomic analysis of cells and wound tissues identifies coordinated regulation of mitochondrial function and oxidative phosphorylation as a central mechanism. In a diabetic rabbit ear model, the hydrogel with US further attenuates hypertrophic scar formation. This programmable piezoelectric hydrogel converts noninvasive US into spatially confined bioelectrical and biochemical cues, offering a promising strategy to overcome multifactorial barriers in diabetic wound healing.
authors: Wang K, Zhuo S, Song B, Chen J, Zhao X, Li S, You S, Jiang D, Chen Y, Dang J, Wang T, Guo B, Yu Z, Song B.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates bidirectional neurogenesis-macrophage crosstalk and neuroimmune-associated signaling in wound healing.
summary_ja: 糖尿病性創傷の治癒遅延は、持続的な炎症や神経免疫クロストークの障害が原因となる。本研究では、超音波活性化によって神経再生とマクロファージの再プログラミングを協調的に制御する、注入可能な圧電ハイドロゲルを開発した。このハイドロゲルは、超音波照射下でM2マクロファージへの分極を促進し、後根神経節ニューロンの軸索伸長を増強して、双方向の神経・マクロファージ相互作用を確立した。2型糖尿病マウスモデルにおいて、創傷閉鎖の加速、再神経支配および血管新生の亢進、コラーゲン再構築の改善が確認された。
summary_en: To address impaired neuro-immune crosstalk in chronic diabetic wounds, researchers developed an injectable, ultrasound-activated piezoelectric hydrogel. In vitro, the hydrogel under ultrasound promoted M2 macrophage polarization and enhanced axonal outgrowth of dorsal root ganglion neurons. In a type II diabetic mouse model, it significantly accelerated wound closure, enhanced reinnervation, and improved tissue remodeling. Transcriptomic analysis suggested that the coordinated regulation of mitochondrial function and oxidative phosphorylation underlies these therapeutic effects.
key_finding_ja: 超音波活性化圧電ハイドロゲルが、M2マクロファージ分極と感覚神経軸索伸長を同時に促進し、糖尿病マウスモデルにおける創傷治癒と再神経支配を著しく加速させることを示した。
why_it_matters_ja: 非侵襲的な超音波を局所的なバイオ電気・生化学シグナルに変換する本技術は、難治性糖尿病性創傷に対する新しい神経免疫標的治療法として応用されることが期待されます。

title: Is amyloid beta peptide a driver of inflammaging?
abstract: Inflammaging, the chronic subclinical systemic inflammation accompanying aging, represents a critical pathogenetic mechanism underlying age-related neurodegenerative diseases. While amyloid beta (Aβ) peptides are established contributors to neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease, their role in aging-related subclinical inflammation remains insufficiently elucidated. In humans, Aβ exhibits dual functions: it supports neuronal activity, survival, and protection against neurotrauma, while also promoting inflammation and central nervous system dysfunction. This review highlights the beneficial effects of Aβ, including its antioxidant and antipathogenic properties, and synthesizes current knowledge of the molecular mechanisms driving Aβ-associated inflammaging. We structure this analysis across distinct brain cell types - microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, neurons, pericytes, and endothelial cells - and consider additional factors influencing Aβ-related neuroinflammation. Finally, we examine strategies to counteract the detrimental effects of Aβ, focusing on Aβ physiological clearance via the blood-brain barrier and glymphatic system, as well as therapeutic interventions. Understanding Aβ-driven inflammaging mechanisms offers new therapeutic avenues for early intervention in age-related neurodegenerative diseases, particularly in genetically susceptible populations. Targeting Aβ-associated inflammaging reframes Aβ not solely as a pathological marker but also as a context-dependent contributor to inflammatory processes during brain aging.
authors: Kechko OI, Moskalev AA, Franceschi C, Mitkevich VA, Makarov AA.
screening_reason: The review explores the role of amyloid beta peptides in driving neuroinflammation and subclinical inflammation (inflammaging) during brain aging.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、加齢に伴う慢性的な亜臨床的全身性炎症である「インフラメイジング（炎症性老化）」におけるアミロイドβ（Aβ）ペプチドの役割を検証している。Aβは神経活動のサポートや抗酸化作用などの有益な機能を持つ一方で、脳の様々な細胞種において炎症を促進する二面性を有している。著者らは、血液脳関門やグリンパ系を介したAβの生理学的クリアランス機構を整理し、Aβに関連する神経炎症を標的とした治療介入の可能性について議論している。
summary_en: This review examines the role of amyloid beta (Aβ) peptides in driving inflammaging, the chronic subclinical systemic inflammation associated with aging. It highlights the dual functions of Aβ, including its beneficial antioxidant and antipathogenic properties alongside its inflammatory effects across various brain cell types. Additionally, the authors discuss physiological clearance mechanisms and potential therapeutic strategies targeting Aβ-associated neuroinflammation.
key_finding_ja: Aβは抗酸化作用や抗病原体作用などの生理的利点を持つ一方で、微小環境や細胞種に応じて加齢に伴う神経炎症（インフラメイジング）を駆動する二面性を持つ。
why_it_matters_ja: Aβを単なる病理学的マーカーではなく文脈依存的な炎症因子として再定義することは、加齢に伴う神経変性疾患の早期介入に向けた新たな治療戦略の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Hippocampal remodeling in chronic pain: Structural, functional, cellular, metabolic, and molecular mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
abstract: Chronic pain is a multifaceted condition characterized by persistent nociceptive signaling and maladaptive central nervous system plasticity, in which the hippocampus has emerged as a critical hub of structural, functional, metabolic, and molecular remodeling. This review systematically synthesizes current evidence on hippocampal alterations in chronic pain across multiple levels, including structural remodeling (e.g., gray matter atrophy and impaired neurogenesis), functional and circuit-level disruptions, metabolic dysregulation, and cellular and molecular mechanisms. In particular, we highlight convergent pathways involving neurotransmitter and receptor dysregulation, cytokine-driven neuroinflammation, neurotrophic signaling deficits, and additional molecular alterations that collectively impair synaptic plasticity and hippocampal network stability. Importantly, we propose a multiscale integrative framework in which synaptic imbalance, neuroimmune activation, and neurotrophic dysregulation interact to drive hippocampal dysfunction, forming a bidirectional loop that links pain, emotion, and cognition. We further discuss therapeutic strategies targeting hippocampal remodeling, including pharmacological, metabolic, neuroimmune, and circuit-level neuromodulation approaches, as well as emerging precision medicine strategies. By integrating preclinical and clinical evidence, this review positions the hippocampus as a central node in chronic pain pathophysiology and a promising target for developing interventions that address both nociceptive and comorbid affective and cognitive symptoms. These insights support a unified model of hippocampal remodeling in chronic pain that may guide future precision diagnostics and targeted interventions.
authors: Zhang Y, Xing X, Chen W, Zheng X, Yu X, Wei X, Feng C, Sun L, Liu Z, Wang D, Wang K.
screening_reason: The review focuses on hippocampal remodeling in chronic pain, highlighting cytokine-driven neuroinflammation and neuroimmune activation as key pathological mechanisms.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、慢性疼痛における海馬の構造的、機能的、代謝的、および分子的な再構築に関する現在の知見を統合している。シナプスの不均衡、神経免疫の活性化、および神経栄養因子の調節障害が相互に作用して海馬の機能障害を引き起こす仕組みを強調している。痛み、感情、認知を結びつける統合的な枠組みを提案し、これらの海馬の変化を標的とした治療戦略について議論している。
summary_en: This review synthesizes current evidence on hippocampal remodeling in chronic pain across structural, functional, metabolic, and molecular levels. It highlights how synaptic imbalance, neuroimmune activation, and neurotrophic dysregulation interact to drive hippocampal dysfunction. The authors propose an integrative framework linking pain, emotion, and cognition, and discuss potential therapeutic strategies targeting these hippocampal alterations.
key_finding_ja: 慢性疼痛における海馬の再構築は、神経免疫活性化やシナプス不均衡などが相互作用する多階層的なプロセスであり、痛みと情動・認知障害を結びつける重要なハブである。
why_it_matters_ja: 慢性疼痛に伴う感覚的症状だけでなく、併発する感情障害や認知機能低下に対する新たな治療標的の同定に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Microbiome-guided cancer immunotherapy: immune mechanisms, resistance pathways, and translational opportunities for precision oncology.
abstract: The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as a modulator of tumor-immune interactions and has been associated with cancer development, progression, and therapeutic response, while direct causal evidence remains strongest in mechanistic and interventional models. Microbial composition and metabolites, including SCFAs, bile acids, inosine, and tryptophan-derived products, may shape host immunity by influencing the tumor microenvironment (TME) and systemic immune responses, although the strength of evidence varies by model system and clinical context. These microbial signals have been linked to changes in T cells, B cells, NK cells, and MDSCs, with mechanistic studies supporting effects on cytokine networks, immune checkpoint signaling, inflammation, and antitumor immunity. Emerging translational evidence indicates that specific microbial signatures may serve as predictive biomarkers for immunotherapy efficacy, resistance, and treatment-related toxicity. In parallel, microbiome-targeted strategies, including FMT, probiotics, prebiotics, dietary modulation, and engineered microbial therapeutics, are being investigated as adjunctive approaches to improve cancer therapy, but their clinical efficacy remains incompletely validated. Understanding microbiome-immune crosstalk may therefore support precision oncology by identifying tractable microbial targets for improving therapeutic outcomes, overcoming immune-mediated treatment resistance, and guiding patient stratification across diverse cancer types and settings in clinical oncology practice.
authors: Amin I, Elgebaly AS, Mohamed HH, Abuelhaded K, Alam-ElDein KM, Ibrahim AK, Farag SA, Adel A, Hamdy M, Elkhawanky M, Mahdy A.
journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
screening_reason: The paper reviews how the gut microbiome and its metabolites modulate tumor-immune interactions and systemic immunity in cancer immunotherapy.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、腸内細菌叢とその代謝物が腫瘍と免疫の相互作用を修飾し、がん免疫療法の治療効果に影響を与える機序を概説している。短鎖脂肪酸や胆汁酸などの微生物由来代謝物が、腫瘍微小環境におけるT細胞やB細胞などの免疫細胞や免疫チェックポイントシグナルに及ぼす影響を説明している。さらに、特定の微生物シグネチャーを予測バイオマーカーとして活用する可能性や、糞便微生物移植（FMT）やプロバイオティクスなどの介入法の現状について議論している。
summary_en: This review explores how the gut microbiome and its metabolites modulate tumor-immune interactions and influence cancer immunotherapy outcomes. It describes the mechanisms by which microbial signals affect various immune cells and checkpoint pathways within the tumor microenvironment. The authors also discuss the potential of microbial signatures as predictive biomarkers and evaluate current microbiome-targeted interventions, such as fecal microbiota transplantation and probiotics.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢とその代謝物は、腫瘍微小環境における免疫細胞やシグナル伝達経路を修飾することで、がん免疫療法の効果や耐性、毒性に影響を与える可能性がある。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌と免疫系の相互作用を解明することは、個別化医療における新たなバイオマーカーの同定や、がん治療効果を向上させるための補助療法の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Impact of microbiome alterations on fracture healing and nonunion: a narrative review.
abstract: Introduction Fracture healing is a complex biological process determined by mechanical stability, vascular supply, and systemic physiological factors. Despite advances in fracture management, nonunion remains an important clinical challenge. Emerging evidence indicates that the gut microbiome is a key regulator of bone metabolism and fracture repair through immune modulation, nutrient digestion, and microbial signaling pathways. Methods We conducted a narrative review synthesizing experimental and clinical evidence on the impact of gut microbiome alterations on fracture healing and nonunion. Literature searches were performed in PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus for studies published between 2013 and 2026. A total of 107 records were initially screened by title and abstract, and 11 studies meeting inclusion criteria were included in the final synthesis. Many screened articles focused on osteoporosis, general bone metabolism or outcomes related to microbiome that didn't evaluate fracture healing, non-union, delayed union, or complications related to fractures, therefore they were excluded. Results The gut microbiome emerges as an important regulator of bone metabolism and fracture repair. Microbial metabolites, particularly short-chain fatty acids, are associated with enhanced osteoblast activity, suppressed osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, and improved calcium absorption, collectively supporting bone mineral density and trabecular integrity. Dysbiosis impairs fracture healing by promoting gut barrier dysfunction, increasing intestinal permeability, and elevating systemic inflammation. Elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-17a, are linked to reduced callus mineralization and delayed bone regeneration. Evidence also suggests a reciprocal interaction, where fracture events can alter gut microbiome composition and function. Microbiome-targeted interventions, such as probiotic and prebiotic supplementation, show therapeutic potential by improving bone microarchitecture, stimulating osteogenic signaling, and mitigating inflammation. Clinically, microbial dysregulation, particularly in infection-associated states, correlates with prolonged healing times and increased bone loss. Conclusions The gut microbiome is an emerging systemic regulator of bone metabolism and may influence fracture healing and nonunion risk through mechanisms that include immune modulation, microbial metabolites, and nutrient metabolism. Dysbiosis may impair bone regeneration and increase the risk of delayed union or nonunion. Microbiome-targeted therapies are promising, but more human studies are needed to confirm their clinical relevance. These findings highlight the interconnected roles of the microbiome, immune function, and metabolism in bone healing, underscoring the need for further research.
authors: Barbaroux TA, Khattak AR, Husain Thamer RASH, Alqanaie M, Patel H, Kambere AJK, Alobaid R, AlShaheen ST, Kazmi S, Alelaimi A, Brendan K, Jawed I.
journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
screening_reason: The review synthesizes evidence on how the gut microbiome and its metabolites (such as short-chain fatty acids) regulate bone metabolism and fracture healing.
summary_ja: 本ナラティブレビューは、腸内細菌叢の変化が骨折治癒および偽関節（骨癒合不全）のリスクに及ぼす影響を検証している。短鎖脂肪酸などの微生物代謝産物が骨修復をサポートする一方で、菌交代症（ディスバイオシス）は腸管透過性の亢進や全身性炎症を引き起こして治癒を阻害することを説明している。また、プロバイオティクスやプレバイオティクスなどの腸内細菌叢を標的とした介入が、骨再生を促進する治療法として有望であることを示している。
summary_en: This narrative review examines the impact of gut microbiome alterations on fracture healing and the risk of nonunion. It describes how microbial metabolites like short-chain fatty acids support bone repair, whereas dysbiosis impairs healing by increasing intestinal permeability and systemic inflammation. The review also highlights the potential of microbiome-targeted interventions, such as probiotics and prebiotics, to improve bone regeneration.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢とその代謝産物は骨代謝と骨折治癒を制御しており、ディスバイオシスは全身性炎症を介して骨再生を阻害し偽関節のリスクを高める可能性がある。
why_it_matters_ja: 骨折治療において、従来の整形外科的アプローチに加えて腸内環境の調整という新たな治療戦略が導入される契機となるかもしれない。

title: Vitamin B12-mediated microglial immunometabolic reprogramming: A novel mechanistic insight into diabetes-associated cognitive impairment.
abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DCI) is an increasingly recognized neurological complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus characterized by chronic neuroinflammation and microglial immunometabolic dysregulation. Vitamin B12 (VB12) deficiency, which is highly prevalent in patients with diabetes, has been strongly associated with cognitive decline, hippocampal atrophy, and white matter injury. Emerging evidence suggests that VB12 plays a critical role in maintaining one‑carbon metabolism, mitochondrial function, and redox homeostasis. Mechanistically, VB12 deficiency promotes homocysteine accumulation, disrupts the S-adenosylmethionine/S-adenosylhomocysteine balance, impairs mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, and enhances oxidative stress, thereby driving pro-inflammatory microglial activation and sustained neuroinflammation. In addition, gut microbiota dysbiosis, particularly reduced abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila and other VB12-producing bacteria, may further impair VB12 bioavailability and aggravate neuroinflammation through the gut-brain axis. This review summarizes current evidence linking VB12 deficiency to microglial immunometabolic remodeling in DCI and discusses the therapeutic potential of targeting VB12 metabolism and gut microbial ecology for preventing diabetes-related cognitive decline.
authors: Zhang X, Li J, An Y, Zheng J, Xu G, Wang J, Chen L, Lu Y.
screening_reason: The review focuses on microglial immunometabolic reprogramming, neuroinflammation, and gut-brain axis interactions in cognitive impairment.
summary_ja: 糖尿病関連認知障害（DCI）は、慢性的な神経炎症とミクログリアの免疫代謝異常を特徴とする合併症である。本総説では、糖尿病患者で頻度の高いビタミンB12（VB12）欠乏が、ミクログリアの炎症性活性化と持続的な神経炎症を引き起こすメカニズムをまとめている。VB12欠乏は、ホモシステインの蓄積やミトコンドリアの酸化的リン酸化の障害、酸化ストレスの増強を介してミクログリアの代謝を再編成する。さらに、Akkermansia muciniphilaなどのVB12産生腸内細菌の減少を伴う腸内細菌叢の乱れが、VB12の生体利用能を低下させ、脳腸軸を介して神経炎症を悪化させる可能性についても議論している。
summary_en: This review highlights the role of vitamin B12 (VB12) deficiency in driving microglial immunometabolic dysregulation and chronic neuroinflammation in diabetes-associated cognitive impairment. VB12 deficiency impairs mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and increases oxidative stress, promoting pro-inflammatory microglial activation. Additionally, gut microbiota dysbiosis, characterized by a reduction in VB12-producing bacteria, may further decrease VB12 bioavailability and exacerbate neuroinflammation via the gut-brain axis. The authors discuss the therapeutic potential of targeting VB12 metabolism and gut microbial ecology to prevent cognitive decline.
key_finding_ja: ビタミンB12欠乏がミクログリアの免疫代謝再編成と炎症性活性化を誘導するメカニズム、および腸内細菌叢の乱れがそれに与える影響を整理した。
why_it_matters_ja: ビタミンB12代謝や腸内細菌叢を標的とした新たなアプローチが、糖尿病に伴う認知機能低下の予防や治療戦略の開発に寄与する可能性があります。

title: Gut-microbiota-brain axis as a potential source of susceptibility/risk biomarkers for post-traumatic epilepsy: An opinion review.
abstract: Both clinical and experimental evidence support the notion that traumatic brain injury (TBI) through the top-down dysregulation of gut-microbiota-brain axis (GMBA) profoundly affects the function and structural integrity of the gut, and that this GMBA dysregulation, in turn may contribute to certain chronic sequelae of TBI, possibly including epilepsy. It is therefore plausible that early post-TBI GMBA perturbations may serve as a source of susceptibility/risk PTE biomarkers derived from TBI-induced intestinal epithelial injury, disruption of intestinal barrier and altered composition and function of gut microbiome. The review particularly focuses on disentangling general biomarkers of TBI-induced intestinal dysfunction from those specifically associated with PTE risk. Although the subject in question is still in its nascent stage, several biomarkers appear promising, such as plasma intestinal fatty acid binding protein, plasma lipopolysaccharide and fecal profiles of gut microbes and their metabolic products, short chain fatty acids. It is concluded that while GMBA-derived biomarkers may not be able alone to stratify PTE risk with high certainty, they may enhance the performance of multimodal predictive models when integrated with other biomarkers in development.
authors: Mazarati AM, Million M, Larauche M, Galanopoulou AS.
screening_reason: The paper is a review focusing on the gut-microbiota-brain axis, specifically how gut microbiome alterations and microbial metabolites (short-chain fatty acids) serve as biomarkers for post-traumatic epilepsy.
summary_ja: 本オピニオンレビューは、頭部外傷（TBI）後の外傷後てんかん（PTE）に対する感受性・リスクバイオマーカーの候補として、腸内細菌叢-脳軸（GMBA）に注目している。TBIによって誘発される腸管機能障害や腸内細菌叢の組成変化が、てんかんなどの慢性的な後遺症に寄与する可能性を議論している。血漿中リポ多糖や糞便中短鎖脂肪酸などのGMBA由来バイオマーカーを多因子予測モデルに統合することで、PTEのリスク評価精度が向上する可能性を提案している。
summary_en: This opinion review discusses the gut-microbiota-brain axis (GMBA) as a potential source of biomarkers for post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) following traumatic brain injury (TBI). It highlights how TBI-induced intestinal dysfunction and altered gut microbiome composition may contribute to chronic sequelae. The authors suggest that integrating GMBA-derived biomarkers, such as plasma lipopolysaccharide and fecal short-chain fatty acids, into multimodal predictive models could improve PTE risk stratification.
key_finding_ja: 頭部外傷後の腸内細菌叢-脳軸の乱れは、外傷後てんかんのリスクを予測するための有望なバイオマーカー源となる可能性がある。
why_it_matters_ja: 外傷後てんかんの早期予測や個別化された予防的介入モデルの構築に寄与することが期待される。

title: Integrative network pharmacology and molecular dynamics analysis of a curcumin-indole-3-propionic acid conjugate for diabetes-associated cognitive decline.
abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive decline (DACD) represents a complex disorder arising from the intersection of metabolic dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and neurodegenerative signaling. Despite increasing clinical recognition, the molecular network governing DACD remains poorly defined, and a systems-level network pharmacology approach has not previously been applied to this condition. Curcumin-indole-3-propionic acid conjugate (CUR-IPA), developed from two bioactive neuroprotective scaffolds, offers a rational multi-target framework to modulate DACD-associated pathways. DACD-related genes were compiled and analyzed using protein-protein interaction networks, hub gene identification, and pathway enrichment analysis. Drug-likeness and ADMET properties of CUR, IPA, and CUR-IPA were predicted in silico. Molecular docking was performed against prioritized targets, followed by 200-ns molecular dynamics simulations. Protein-ligand stability and dynamics were assessed using RMSD, RMSF, DCCM, elastic network model, and Markov state model analyses. Binding energetics were quantified using MM-PBSA calculations with residue-level decomposition. Network pharmacology identified PSEN1 and TGFβ1 as central hub proteins linking amyloid regulation, neuronal maintenance, immune signaling, and metabolic pathways in DACD. CUR-IPA satisfied multiple drug-likeness filters and exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles. Docking and MD simulations demonstrated stable binding of CUR-IPA within the active sites of PSEN1 and TGFβ1. ENM revealed restricted collective motions around ligand-binding regions, while MSM analysis identified energetically favorable and kinetically stable conformational states. MM-PBSA calculations confirmed strong binding affinities driven by key catalytic residues. This study establishes the first network pharmacology framework for DACD and demonstrates that CUR-IPA acts as a stable, multi-target modulator of key neurodegenerative and metabolic pathways.
authors: Sidhambaram J, Iruthayaraj A, Viswaresh Babu S, Thayumanavan P.
screening_reason: The paper investigates a therapeutic conjugate for diabetes-associated cognitive decline, focusing on its ability to modulate neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative signaling.
summary_ja: 本研究は、ネットワーク薬理学と分子動力学シミュレーションを用いて、糖尿病関連認知機能低下（DACD）に対するクルクミン-インドール-3-プロピオン酸抱合体（CUR-IPA）の治療効果を評価した。インシリコ解析により、アミロイド制御、神経維持、免疫シグナル伝達を繋ぐ中心的なハブタンパク質としてPSEN1およびTGFβ1が同定された。シミュレーションの結果、CUR-IPAは良好な薬物様特性と薬物動態プロファイルを示し、標的タンパク質に対して安定した結合能を有することが示された。
summary_en: This study utilizes network pharmacology and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate a curcumin-indole-3-propionic acid conjugate (CUR-IPA) for treating diabetes-associated cognitive decline (DACD). The in silico analysis identified PSEN1 and TGFβ1 as key hub proteins linking amyloid regulation, neuronal maintenance, and immune signaling. Simulations demonstrated that CUR-IPA exhibits favorable drug-likeness, pharmacokinetic profiles, and stable binding to these target proteins.
key_finding_ja: インシリコ解析および分子動力学シミュレーションにより、CUR-IPAがPSEN1およびTGFβ1を標的として安定に結合し、DACDに関与する神経変性および代謝経路を調節し得ることが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 糖尿病に伴う認知機能低下の分子ネットワークを標的としたこの多標的アプローチは、代謝異常と神経炎症が交差する複雑な疾患に対する新規治療薬候補の設計に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Intratumoral Hypoxia Triggers Mitochondrial BHLHE40 ROS Sensing Pathway to Promote Radioresistance in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
abstract: Intratumoral hypoxia is a hallmark of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and induces complex biological responses, including treatment resistance and mitochondrial production of reactive oxygen species (ROS). However, the direct mechanisms through which hypoxia-induced ROS are sensed and contribute to therapeutic resistance remain elusive. ROS can regulate the function of transcription factors through oxidation of cysteine thiol groups, but the compartmentalization limits their physical interaction with transcription factors. Here, BHLHE40, a transcription factor traditionally recognized for its nuclear function, is identified as a novel mitochondrial sensor of hypoxia-induced ROS. Mitochondrial BHLHE40 experiences ROS-dependent oxidation of cysteine thiol groups and forms disulfide-linked homodimers. In addition to post-translational modification that regulates BHLHE40 protein levels, hypoxia also increases BHLHE40 mRNA levels through hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs)-dependent transcriptional activation. These dual mechanisms of modulating BHLHE40 ensure its rapid elevation during the early stage of hypoxia. Functionally, BHLHE40 plays a critical role in hypoxia-induced radioresistance through transcriptional activation of cellular antioxidant systems and inhibition of cytotoxic effects mediated by irradiation-generated ROS. This study reveals a previously unrecognized role of BHLHE40 in sensing and regulating ROS in response to hypoxia, and highlights its potential as a therapeutic target to overcome hypoxia-promoted radioresistance in TNBC.
authors: Liu J, Nie Z, Chen X, Ji G, Zhang Y, Zhao Z, Zhang Y, Du X, Zhou Z, Li J, Yang Y, Sun F, Yan Z, Lu H.
screening_reason: The study details a mechanistic post-translational modification where hypoxia-induced ROS trigger the oxidation of cysteine thiol groups on BHLHE40 to form disulfide-linked homodimers.
summary_ja: 著者らは、トリプルネガティブ乳がんにおいて、転写因子BHLHE40が低酸素誘導性の活性酸素種（ROS）を感知する新規のミトコンドリアセンサーであることを同定した。低酸素条件下において、BHLHE40はシステイン残基のチオール基のROS依存的な酸化を受け、ジスルフィド結合によるホモ二量体を形成するという翻訳後修飾を受ける。このミトコンドリアでの感知機構と転写活性化の二重の機序により、低酸素初期にBHLHE40が急速に増加し、抗酸化システムを活性化することで放射線耐性を促進することが示された。
summary_en: The authors identified the transcription factor BHLHE40 as a novel mitochondrial sensor of hypoxia-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) in triple-negative breast cancer. Under hypoxic conditions, BHLHE40 undergoes ROS-dependent oxidation of cysteine thiol groups to form disulfide-linked homodimers, representing a key post-translational modification. This mitochondrial sensing mechanism, combined with transcriptional activation, rapidly elevates BHLHE40 levels to promote radioresistance by activating antioxidant systems.
key_finding_ja: BHLHE40は低酸素誘導性ROSを感知してシステイン残基の酸化（翻訳後修飾）を介して二量体化し、抗酸化システムを活性化することでトリプルネガティブ乳がんの放射線耐性を促進する。
why_it_matters_ja: 低酸素環境におけるROS感知と翻訳後修飾を介した放射線耐性獲得の新たな分子機構が解明されたことで、トリプルネガティブ乳がんの治療抵抗性を克服するための新たな治療標的となる可能性がある。

title: Improved comprehensive profiling of fecal bile acids through chemical derivatization combined with HPLC-MS/MS analysis.
abstract: Bile acids (BAs) facilitate the digestion and absorption of fats and influence lipid and glucose homeostasis, making them potential therapeutic targets for obesity and related metabolic disorders. The liver and intestinal microbiota modify BAs structurally, generating diverse chemical forms and isomers. Comprehensive profiling of the BA pool is critical for understanding their key biological functions and as a therapeutic approach for related diseases. High-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) is usually chosen as the preferred method for BA detection due to the complex chemical structures, the wide range of actual concentrations and the complexity of fecal sample matrices. However, free BAs are difficult to ionize, resulting in low detection signals and a lack of characteristic structural fragments to assist in structural identification. In this method, the labeling reagent (2-aminoethyl) trimethylammonium (AETMA) is employed to label the carboxyl group of BAs. Compared with underivatized BAs, the detection sensitivity of unconjugated BAs was enhanced by 25-180 fold, while that of conjugated BAs increased by 6-160 fold. It also generates unique fragment ions and enhances MS response, facilitating the discovery of potential BAs. Methodological parameters were validated using 38 BAs as representatives. Through methodological validation, it was verified that the precision, recovery, matrix effect and stability parameters of the method met acceptable criteria. We also identified 61 confirmed BAs and 55 additional candidate BAs in human pooled fecal samples. It has been successfully applied to fecal BA analysis in obese populations, providing valuable insights into potential therapeutic strategies for obesity.
authors: Wang Y, Chen Y, Ling Q, Zhao L, Xiong X.
journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
screening_reason: The paper describes a method for profiling fecal bile acids, which are key products of host-microbial co-metabolism in the gut.
summary_ja: 著者らは、糞便中の胆汁酸を包括的にプロファイリングするため、化学誘導体化試薬AETMAを用いた改良型HPLC-MS/MS法を開発した。この誘導体化技術により、遊離型胆汁酸の検出感度が25〜180倍、抱合型胆汁酸の検出感度が6〜160倍向上した。開発された手法は精度、回収率、安定性などのバリデーション基準を満たし、ヒトの混合糞便サンプルから61種類の確定された胆汁酸と55種類の候補を同定することに成功した。
summary_en: The authors developed an improved HPLC-MS/MS method using (2-aminoethyl) trimethylammonium (AETMA) chemical derivatization for the comprehensive profiling of fecal bile acids. This derivatization significantly enhanced the detection sensitivity of both unconjugated and conjugated bile acids. The method was validated for precision, recovery, and stability, and successfully identified numerous bile acids in human fecal samples, including those from obese individuals.
key_finding_ja: AETMAを用いた化学誘導体化とHPLC-MS/MSを組み合わせることで、糞便中の遊離型および抱合型胆汁酸の検出感度が大幅に向上し、多数の胆汁酸の同定が可能となった。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌によって修飾される胆汁酸プロファイルを高感度に分析できるこの技術は、肥満などの代謝性疾患における病態解明や新たな治療標的の探索に貢献することが期待される。

title: Modulating Stress Granules via HDAC6 Inhibition: A Promising Strategy against Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that dysregulated cellular stress responses, particularly the formation and persistence of stress granules (SGs), may significantly contribute to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis. SGs are dynamic, membrane-less ribonucleoprotein assemblies that sequester stalled translation preinitiation complexes during cellular stress. Under physiological conditions, SGs are transient and disassemble upon stress resolution, often facilitated by heat shock proteins (HSPs). However, under chronic stress, persistent or aberrant SGs can form, which may seed pathological protein aggregation and exacerbate proteostatic imbalance, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration. Despite the growing body of evidence linking HDAC6 to SG dynamics and AD pathology, the precise mechanistic relationship remains unresolved. This review highlights the current understanding of HDAC6-mediated SG regulation in AD, identifies critical knowledge gaps, and discusses the therapeutic potential of selective HDAC6 inhibition in modulating SG pathology and neuroinflammation.
authors: Jagaselvan E, Mondal P, Zhang C.
screening_reason: The review focuses on the therapeutic potential of modulating stress granules to alleviate neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: ストレス顆粒（SG）は、細胞ストレス時に翻訳開始前複合体を隔離する一過性のリボヌクレオタンパク質複合体ですが、慢性的なストレス下では持続的または異常なSGが形成されます。このような異常なSGは、病的なタンパク質凝集の起点となり、プロテオスタシスの崩壊、神経炎症、および神経変性を悪化させ、アルツハイマー病（AD）の病態に関与することが示唆されています。HDAC6はSGのダイナミクスやAD病態への関与が指摘されているものの、その詳細な分子メカニズムは未だ解明されていません。本総説では、ADにおけるHDAC6を介したSG制御に関する現在の知見を整理し、選択的HDAC6阻害によるSG病態および神経炎症の抑制という治療戦略の可能性を議論しています。
summary_en: Persistent or aberrant stress granules (SGs) under chronic stress can seed pathological protein aggregation, exacerbating proteostatic imbalance, neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Although HDAC6 is implicated in SG dynamics and AD pathology, the precise underlying molecular mechanisms remain unresolved. This review synthesizes current understanding of HDAC6-mediated SG regulation and discusses the therapeutic potential of selective HDAC6 inhibition to modulate SG pathology and neuroinflammation.
key_finding_ja: アルツハイマー病の病態において、持続的なストレス顆粒の形成が神経炎症や神経変性を悪化させており、HDAC6の選択的阻害がその制御に向けた有望な治療標的として注目されている。
why_it_matters_ja: ストレス顆粒のダイナミクスを標的とすることで、従来の治療アプローチとは異なる、神経炎症やプロテオスタシス異常を伴う神経変性疾患の新たな治療法開発につながる可能性があります。

title: Isoform-selective HSP90 inhibition as a precision therapeutic strategy for neurodegenerative and metabolic diseases.
abstract: Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) is a central regulator of cellular proteostasis, coordinating the folding, stabilization, and turnover of a wide range of client proteins in the cytosol, endoplasmic reticulum, and mitochondria. Accumulating evidence indicates that the four HSP90 paralogs HSP90α, HSP90β, GRP94, and TRAP1 have distinct pathological roles in neurodegenerative and metabolic diseases. In neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, aberrant HSP90 activity contributes to the persistence of toxic protein conformers, defective autophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction, and chronic neuroinflammation. In metabolic disorders such as obesity, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, GRP94- and TRAP1-dependent signaling promotes endoplasmic reticulum stress, impaired mitochondrial metabolism, insulin resistance, and inflammatory remodeling. These mechanistic insights have accelerated the development of a new generation of HSP90 inhibitors with improved selectivity, tissue targeting, and brain penetration. Unlike earlier pan-HSP90 inhibitors, these compounds are designed to exploit paralog-specific vulnerabilities and may enable safer long-term modulation of disease-relevant chaperone networks. This review summarizes current advances in the biology and pharmacology of HSP90 paralogs and proposes isoform-selective HSP90 targeting as a promising therapeutic strategy at the intersection of neurodegeneration and metabolic dysfunction.
authors: Alanazi SM, Al-Kuraishy HM, Alexiou A, Papadakis M, Faheem SA, Batiha GE.
screening_reason: The paper reviews the role of HSP90 paralogs in neurodegenerative and metabolic diseases, specifically highlighting their contribution to chronic neuroinflammation.
summary_ja: 熱ショックタンパク質90（HSP90）は、細胞のプロテオスタシスを制御する中心的な因子であり、その4つのパラログは神経変性疾患や代謝性疾患において異なる病理学的役割を担っています。神経変性疾患では、異常なHSP90活性が毒性タンパク質の蓄積や慢性的な神経炎症に寄与しています。一方、代謝性疾患では、GRP94およびTRAP1依存的なシグナル伝達が小胞体ストレスやインスリン抵抗性を促進します。本総説では、これらパラログ特異的な脆弱性を標的とする、組織移行性や脳移行性に優れた次世代のアイソフォーム選択的HSP90阻害剤の開発状況と治療戦略としての可能性をまとめています。
summary_en: Heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) paralogs play distinct pathological roles in neurodegenerative and metabolic diseases. In neurodegenerative disorders, aberrant HSP90 activity contributes to toxic protein accumulation and chronic neuroinflammation, while in metabolic disorders, GRP94- and TRAP1-dependent signaling promotes endoplasmic reticulum stress and insulin resistance. This review highlights recent advances in developing isoform-selective HSP90 inhibitors with improved selectivity and brain penetration as a promising therapeutic strategy.
key_finding_ja: HSP90の各パラログは神経変性疾患と代謝性疾患において異なる病理作用を持っており、アイソフォーム選択的な阻害剤の開発が新たな治療戦略として期待されている。
why_it_matters_ja: 従来のパンHSP90阻害剤に伴う毒性を回避しつつ、神経炎症や代謝異常を安全かつ長期的に制御できる精密医療の実現につながる可能性があります。

title: Label-Free Evaluation of Advanced Glycation End Products by a Comprehensive Biophysical Analysis.
abstract: Nonenzymatic glycation is a post-translational modification of proteins, leading to the formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) implicated in diabetes, neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), and aging-related complications. The sensitive and precise detection of protein-bound AGEs is essential for comprehending their pathological implications. Conventional detection methods for AGEs have several drawbacks, such as being expensive and time-consuming, complex sample preparation steps, etc. Further, AGEs' structural complexity and heterogeneity affect their accurate determination. Therefore, we introduce an autofluorescence-based methodology (LED-induced autofluorescence) for detecting and tracking the formation of AGEs on proteins using a low-power fiber-coupled near-UV LED (340 nm) and a blue LED (430 nm) as excitation sources covering the heterogeneous excitation maxima of multiple AGEs that form on proteins. The device captures the wide range of AGEs-specific autofluorescence signatures without the interference of protein autofluorescence, revealing their heterogeneous composition on proteins. The device demonstrated high sensitivity in detecting standard pentosidine (3.66 pg/μL) at 340 nm excitation, while enabling effective monitoring of the formation and progression of clinically relevant AGEs such as pentosidine, argpyrimidine, vesperlysine (A, B, and C), etc., generated on various structurally distinct glycated proteins in vitro. While noninvasive diabetes risk assessment and diagnosis based on AGEs fluorescence is gaining growing attention, the use of low-power, cost-effective light-emitting diodes (LEDs) as excitation sources offers significant advantages. Their stable power output ensures high reproducibility, enabling a rapid and reliable approach to assessing protein glycation, facilitating the routine monitoring of accumulation of AGEs, and advancing research addressing glycation-related complications in diabetes, aging, and NDDs.
authors: K A, Mukunda DC, Chandra S, Basha S, Biswas S, Mazumder N, Prabhu V, Prabhu MM, Rodrigues J, Hsu CW, Lai SB, Patil A, Chang CY, Zhuo GY, Mahato KK.
screening_reason: The paper presents a biophysical method to detect and track advanced glycation end products (AGEs), which are formed by nonenzymatic glycation, a key post-translational modification.
summary_ja: 非酵素的糖化はタンパク質の翻訳後修飾の一種であり、糖尿病や神経変性疾患、加齢に伴う合併症に関与する後期糖化反応終末産物（AGEs）を形成します。本研究では、低出力の近紫外および青色LEDを励起光源として用いた、ラベルフリーで高感度なLED誘起自家蛍光測定法を開発しました。この装置は、タンパク質自体の背景蛍光に干渉されることなく、多様なAGEs特異的な自家蛍光シグナルを捉えることができます。これにより、in vitroで生成された様々な糖化タンパク質上のペントシジンなどのAGEsの形成および進行を迅速かつ高精度にモニタリングすることが可能となりました。
summary_en: Nonenzymatic glycation is a post-translational modification that forms advanced glycation end products (AGEs) linked to diabetes and neurodegenerative disorders. This study introduces a label-free, LED-induced autofluorescence methodology using low-power near-UV and blue LEDs to detect and track various protein-bound AGEs. The device successfully captured heterogeneous AGEs-specific autofluorescence signatures with high sensitivity and reproducibility without interference from protein autofluorescence.
key_finding_ja: 低出力LEDを励起光源とした自家蛍光測定技術により、タンパク質自体の蛍光に干渉されることなく、多様なAGEsの形成を高感度かつ迅速に検出・追跡することに成功した。
why_it_matters_ja: 糖尿病リスクの非侵襲的評価や、加齢および神経変性疾患における糖化関連合併症の研究を促進する、安価で信頼性の高い日常的モニタリング手法となる可能性があります。
